data.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
data.description: User input is directly concatenated into SQL query string without parameterization. An attacker could inject malicious SQL statements to access, modify, or delete database records.
data.code: const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '${req.params.id}'`;
data.suggestion: Use parameterized queries or an ORM to prevent SQL injection.

data.title: Hardcoded API Secret Key
data.description: API secret key is hardcoded directly in source code. If this code is committed to version control, the secret will be exposed to anyone with repository access.
data.suggestion: Move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager like AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault.

data.title: N+1 Query Pattern Detected
data.description: Database queries are executed inside a loop, causing N+1 query performance degradation. For 1000 users, this generates 1001 database queries instead of 2.
data.suggestion: Use a single JOIN query or batch loading to eliminate the N+1 pattern. Estimated improvement: ~95% reduction in query count.

data.title: Unsafe eval() with User Input
data.description: The eval() function is called with user-controlled input, allowing arbitrary code execution. An attacker could execute malicious JavaScript on the server.
data.suggestion: Replace eval() with a safe expression parser like math.js or expr-eval.

data.title: Insecure Deserialization
data.description: Untrusted data is deserialized using pickle without validation. An attacker could craft a malicious payload to execute arbitrary code during deserialization.
data.suggestion: Use safe serialization formats like JSON or implement strict type checking. For ML models, use safetensors or ONNX format.

data.title: Memory Leak in Event Listener
data.description: Event listeners are registered in useEffect without cleanup. Over time, this causes memory to grow unbounded as listeners accumulate.
data.suggestion: Add cleanup function to useEffect to remove event listeners on unmount.

data.title: Missing CSRF Protection
data.description: State-changing endpoints do not implement CSRF token validation. Attackers could trick authenticated users into performing unintended actions.
data.suggestion: Implement CSRF tokens using csurf middleware or SameSite cookie attributes.

data.title: Unoptimized Tensor Operations
data.description: Tensor operations are performed on CPU instead of GPU, and intermediate tensors are not freed. This wastes ~2.4GB of GPU memory and slows inference by 8x.
data.suggestion: Move operations to GPU with .to('cuda'), use torch.no_grad() for inference, and detach tensors after use. Estimated memory savings: ~2.4GB.

data.title: Weak Password Hashing (MD5)
data.description: Passwords are hashed using MD5, which is cryptographically broken. Rainbow table attacks can crack MD5 hashes in seconds.
data.suggestion: Use bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 for password hashing with proper salt rounds.

data.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability
data.description: File path is constructed using user input without sanitization. An attacker could use '../' sequences to access files outside the intended directory.
data.suggestion: Validate and sanitize filename input. Use path.basename() to strip directory traversal sequences.

data.title: Redundant Re-renders in Component Tree
data.description: Parent component re-renders cause unnecessary re-renders of 12 child components due to missing memoization. This creates noticeable UI lag on data updates.
data.suggestion: Wrap component with React.memo() and memoize callbacks with useCallback(). Use useMemo() for expensive data transformations.

data.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Auth Endpoints
data.description: Authentication endpoints lack rate limiting, enabling brute-force password attacks. An attacker could attempt thousands of password combinations per second.
data.suggestion: Implement rate limiting using express-rate-limit with a maximum of 5 attempts per minute per IP.

data.title: Fix: Parameterized SQL Query
data.before:
const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '${req.params.id}'`;
const result = await db.execute(query);
data.after:
const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?';
const result = await db.execute(query, [req.params.id]);
data.explanation: Replaced string interpolation with parameterized query placeholder. The database driver now handles proper escaping, preventing SQL injection attacks.

data.title: Fix: Environment Variable for Secret Key
data.explanation: Moved the hardcoded secret to an environment variable with a runtime check. The secret should be stored in a .env file (excluded from version control) or a secrets manager.

data.title: Fix: Safe Deserialization with Safetensors
data.after:
from safetensors.torch import load_file

# Validate file extension
if not filepath.endswith('.safetensors'):
    raise ValueError('Only .safetensors format is accepted')
model_state = load_file(filepath)
model.load_state_dict(model_state)
data.explanation: Replaced unsafe pickle deserialization with safetensors format, which cannot execute arbitrary code. Added file extension validation as an additional safety check.

data.title: Fix: Bcrypt Password Hashing
data.explanation: Replaced MD5 hashing with bcrypt, which is designed for password hashing. Salt rounds of 12 provide a good balance between security and performance (~250ms per hash).
